items.criterion: Task category is one of the currently open categories: Science, Software, ML, Operations, Security, Hardware, Media
items.why_it_matters: The category-status page says all listed Terminus 3 categories are open for new submissions.
items.how_to_check: Inspect task configuration, README, or instructions for a category value and confirm it matches one of the open categories.

items.criterion: Task is not a milestone task
items.why_it_matters: The category-status page says milestone tasks are not part of this edition.
items.how_to_check: Search file names and task text for milestone-task framing or milestone-specific submission language.

items.criterion: Task does not require a GPU
items.why_it_matters: The category-status page says GPU tasks are not allowed, though CPU-simulated or compile-only kernel work can be authorable.
items.how_to_check: Inspect Docker, dependency, and instruction files for required CUDA, GPU hardware, or GPU-only execution assumptions.

items.criterion: Task components exclude canary strings
items.why_it_matters: The category-status page says canary strings are excluded from all components.
items.how_to_check: Search all text files for canary-string markers or instructions that identify hidden canaries.

items.criterion: Verifier isolation is configured with environment_mode = "separate"
items.why_it_matters: The category-status page says verifier isolation is required.
items.how_to_check: Search configuration files for environment_mode and verify the value is "separate".

items.criterion: Verifier artifacts are declared as a top-level task.toml key
items.why_it_matters: CI guidance warns that artifacts nested under [verifier] are silently dropped, so the verifier receives nothing.
items.how_to_check: Inspect task.toml and confirm artifacts is declared at the top level, not inside [verifier].

items.criterion: task.toml contains required Terminus 3 metadata and explanation fields
items.why_it_matters: Task Components and CI docs require Terminus 3 metadata fields for packaging, taxonomy, rubric, and review context.
items.how_to_check: Inspect task.toml for [metadata], category, subcategory, tags, difficulty, expert_time_estimate_hours, and explanation fields.

items.criterion: Agent timeout is between 1800 and 18000 seconds
items.why_it_matters: The category-status page gives 1800 seconds as the minimum and 18000 seconds as the ceiling.
items.how_to_check: Search configuration files for timeout fields and confirm the agent timeout is within the allowed range.

items.criterion: Internet access is intentionally configured as network_mode = "public" or "no-network"
items.why_it_matters: The category-status page says public networking is the default and no-network is used when a task should run offline.
items.how_to_check: Search configuration files for network_mode and confirm the setting matches the task's intended online or offline behavior.

items.criterion: Submission targets the Terminus-3-Prod project
items.why_it_matters: The quick-start and CLI docs identify Terminus-3-Prod as the project for task submission.
items.how_to_check: Inspect README, submission notes, or CLI metadata for Terminus-3-Prod.

items.criterion: Starter-template placeholders such as REPLACE are removed
items.why_it_matters: The platform submission docs describe the skeleton as a starter that must be renamed and filled in.
items.how_to_check: Search all readable files for REPLACE, TODO, placeholder task names, or unchanged skeleton language.

items.criterion: Required task files and directories are present
items.why_it_matters: Task component docs define the expected task package structure.
items.how_to_check: Inspect the ZIP for task configuration, instructions, Docker/environment files, oracle/reference solution, and verifier/test files.

items.criterion: tests/Dockerfile is included for the separate verifier image
items.why_it_matters: Terminus 3 runs the verifier in a separate container built from tests/Dockerfile.
items.how_to_check: Inspect the ZIP file list for tests/Dockerfile.

items.criterion: tests/test.sh follows the canonical verifier entrypoint behavior
items.why_it_matters: Platform submission docs say tests/test.sh is the canonical verifier entrypoint and should write reward output rather than exiting early.
items.how_to_check: Inspect tests/test.sh for reward.txt handling, exit 0 at the end, and absence of set -e.

items.criterion: Task instructions clearly state the goal, constraints, and expected deliverable
items.why_it_matters: Task quality docs emphasize clear instructions and unambiguous success criteria.
items.how_to_check: Read instruction.md or README and confirm it explains what the agent must do, what constraints apply, and what output/state is expected.

items.criterion: Task is domain-grounded and targets a genuinely difficult coding-agent workflow
items.why_it_matters: The welcome and quality docs define Terminus 3 as expert-authored, domain-grounded coding-agent evaluation.
items.how_to_check: Read instructions and included files to verify the task requires specialized domain understanding and concrete system manipulation.

items.criterion: Task is not a trivial formatting, search, or boilerplate edit
items.why_it_matters: Difficulty and quality docs expect tasks that challenge frontier coding agents.
items.how_to_check: Assess whether solving requires multi-step reasoning, implementation, debugging, or domain-specific changes rather than simple text edits.

items.criterion: Task includes evidence or rationale for its expected difficulty tier
items.why_it_matters: Difficulty docs define tiers based on empirical agent pass rates and near-miss patterns.
items.how_to_check: Inspect README, metadata, or author notes for difficulty rationale, expected failure modes, or validation notes.

items.criterion: Task category, subcategory, and tags align with the Terminus taxonomy
items.why_it_matters: Task taxonomy docs define the accepted categories and subcategory framing.
items.how_to_check: Compare task metadata and instructions with the taxonomy docs and confirm the chosen category is coherent.

items.criterion: An oracle or reference solution is included
items.why_it_matters: Creating-task docs list writing oracle solutions as part of task authoring.
items.how_to_check: Inspect the ZIP for solution files or documentation that demonstrate correct task completion.

items.criterion: Oracle solution represents a correct solution, not merely a passing artifact
items.why_it_matters: Oracle-solution docs warn that a passing oracle does not itself prove correctness.
items.how_to_check: Read the oracle and tests to confirm the reference implements the intended semantics and is not tailored only to visible checks.

items.criterion: Verifier or test files check semantics rather than appearance
items.why_it_matters: Testing docs say verifiers should check meaningful task outcomes, not superficial formatting.
items.how_to_check: Inspect tests/verifier files and confirm they validate semantic behavior or final state.

items.criterion: Verifier rejects at least one deliberately wrong or shortcut solution
items.why_it_matters: CI feedback and writing-tests docs emphasize rejecting wrong solutions, not only accepting the oracle.
items.how_to_check: Look for negative tests, wrong-solution notes, or local validation evidence that a bad solution fails.

items.criterion: Ground truth is not read from paths the agent can modify
items.why_it_matters: Writing-tests guidance warns against agent-writable ground truth and staging leaks.
items.how_to_check: Inspect verifier/test paths and fixtures to ensure expected answers are fixed outside agent-controlled outputs.

items.criterion: Verifier does not rely only on proxy checks such as file existence or unchanged strings
items.why_it_matters: Testing docs warn that proxy checks can accept shortcuts without validating correctness.
items.how_to_check: Inspect assertions to confirm they validate computed behavior, content semantics, or system state.

items.criterion: Verifier does not grade an old or unrebuilt binary/artifact
items.why_it_matters: Writing-tests docs warn against grading stale artifacts instead of the agent's changed work.
items.how_to_check: Check test setup/build commands to confirm tests rebuild or run against the submitted workspace.

items.criterion: Verifier covers tolerances, optimization objectives, and tie-break behavior when relevant
items.why_it_matters: Recent guidance calls out tolerance drift and untested objectives as review risks.
items.how_to_check: Inspect tests for edge cases, numeric tolerances, objective comparisons, or tie-break assertions relevant to the task.

items.criterion: Tests are deterministic and do not rely on flaky timing, randomness, or external state
items.why_it_matters: CI and validation docs require reliable automated evaluation.
items.how_to_check: Inspect tests for uncontrolled randomness, timeouts, network dependencies, or environment-sensitive assumptions.

items.criterion: Local validation or CI feedback has been run and documented
items.why_it_matters: Submission and CI training docs instruct authors to validate before submission.
items.how_to_check: Look for README notes, logs, or checklist evidence that local validation, oracle, NOP, or CI-style checks were run.

items.criterion: Docker/environment setup is included and suitable for the task
items.why_it_matters: Docker environment docs describe containerized task execution as part of the workflow.
items.how_to_check: Inspect Dockerfile, environment config, dependency files, and setup scripts.

items.criterion: Dockerfile follows documented requirements and avoids unnecessary heavyweight setup
items.why_it_matters: Dockerfile requirements docs describe packaging expectations for reproducible environments.
items.how_to_check: Inspect Dockerfile for pinned/base image choices, install steps, cache behavior, and unnecessary services.

items.criterion: Dockerfile FROM images are digest-pinned
items.why_it_matters: Platform and Dockerfile docs require digest-pinned base images for reproducible task environments.
items.how_to_check: Inspect every Dockerfile FROM line and confirm it uses an @sha256 digest.

items.criterion: Python package installs in Docker/test scripts pin exact versions
items.why_it_matters: CI guidance says unpinned pip, uv pip, and uvx --with installs can drift after the task is authored.
items.how_to_check: Inspect Dockerfiles and test scripts for pip/uv installs and confirm package versions are pinned with ==.

items.criterion: Dockerfiles do not pin a CPU architecture with FROM --platform
items.why_it_matters: CI guidance says tasks should be portable across architectures and must not pin Docker build platform.
items.how_to_check: Search Dockerfiles for FROM --platform.

items.criterion: Dockerfiles and scripts do not call bare nproc for parallelism
items.why_it_matters: CI guidance warns that bare nproc can read host CPU count and over-parallelize inside constrained containers.
items.how_to_check: Search Dockerfiles, tests/test.sh, and solution scripts for nproc usage.

items.criterion: Task does not require privileged Docker or unsafe container flags
items.why_it_matters: Quality guidelines say Terminus tasks must not require root-level privileges or unsafe Docker settings like --privileged.
items.how_to_check: Search compose files, task.toml, Docker scripts, and instructions for --privileged, privileged: true, or unsafe docker_flags.

items.criterion: Runtime and test dependencies are declared in files included in the ZIP
items.why_it_matters: Environment setup docs require dependencies to be reproducible inside the container.
items.how_to_check: Look for pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, package.json, lockfiles, environment files, or Docker install commands.

items.criterion: Environment files do not contain hidden instructions, solution hints, or AI-framework scaffolding
items.why_it_matters: Reviewer checklist and changelog guidance call out hidden environment hints and files such as CLAUDE.md or skills.md as high-severity cleanup issues.
items.how_to_check: Search the ZIP for CLAUDE.md, skills.md, AGENTS.md, hidden instruction files, walkthroughs, or solution-guide language.

items.criterion: Task does not depend on hidden local files, private services, or undeclared external resources
items.why_it_matters: Validation docs require tasks to run in the provided environment.
items.how_to_check: Search instructions, tests, and config for absolute local paths, private URLs, missing datasets, or secret requirements.

items.criterion: ZIP contains only relevant task files and excludes caches, build artifacts, and local secrets
items.why_it_matters: Submission checklist docs expect clean upload packages.
items.how_to_check: Inspect file list for __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .git, node_modules, secrets, credentials, large generated artifacts, or editor junk.

items.criterion: Task materials do not instruct contributors to contact reviewers directly
items.why_it_matters: The portal banner warns that messaging reviewers will not speed review.
items.how_to_check: Search instructions and README for reviewer-contact language or private escalation instructions.

items.criterion: Task is ready for reviewer checklist inspection
items.why_it_matters: Reviewer docs describe common errors and checklist-based review expectations.
items.how_to_check: Confirm instructions, config, oracle, tests, environment, and submission notes are internally consistent before upload.

items.criterion: Rubric or evaluation notes are present when the task requires nuanced judgment
items.why_it_matters: Rubrics and review docs help reviewers understand intended pass/fail boundaries.
items.how_to_check: Look for rubric, README, or task notes explaining acceptance criteria and edge cases.

items.criterion: Known FAQ/troubleshooting issues are addressed in task docs or setup
items.why_it_matters: Reference docs collect common setup and submission issues.
items.how_to_check: Inspect README and setup notes for Docker, CLI, dependency, timeout, or platform-submission gotchas relevant to the task.

items.criterion: Kernel or accelerator tasks are CPU-simulated or compile-only
items.why_it_matters: The taxonomy says Kernels tasks are in scope only when they do not require GPU execution.
items.how_to_check: If the task is a Kernels task, inspect instructions, Dockerfile, and tests for CPU simulation or compile-only validation.
items.applies_when: Only when category/subcategory is Kernels or accelerator/kernel work is mentioned.

items.criterion: Multi-container tasks are tagged under metadata
items.why_it_matters: Quality guidelines say tasks that run multiple containers must be tagged under metadata in task.toml.
items.how_to_check: If the ZIP defines multiple services or containers, inspect task.toml for appropriate metadata tags.
items.applies_when: Only when the task uses multiple containers or service definitions.

items.criterion: Performance thresholds are not set too tightly relative to the oracle
items.why_it_matters: Quality guidelines warn against thresholds so tight they require replicating the oracle.
items.how_to_check: If the task grades performance, inspect verifier thresholds and oracle notes for reasonable slack.
items.applies_when: Only when verifier grades performance, speed, latency, throughput, or optimization quality.

items.criterion: Failed agent runs write 0 to the reward file
items.why_it_matters: Quality guidelines say failed agent runs must write 0 to the reward file instead of exiting first.
items.how_to_check: If the task uses a reward file, inspect test.sh or verifier logic for failure-path reward writing.
items.applies_when: Only when the task uses a reward file.

items.criterion: Environment variables used in test.sh have compatible defaults
items.why_it_matters: Quality guidelines require environment variables in test.sh to have defaults compatible with the task structure.
items.how_to_check: If test.sh uses environment variables, inspect default assignments and fallback values.
items.applies_when: Only when test.sh or verifier scripts use environment variables.
